Interesting thing in law is the "thin-skulled plaintiff". This dictates that if any small action leads to significant damage the abuser is held liable. The example is that if you were to lightly push someone who had a thin-skull and a small impact on the unprotected brain caused death, the pusher would be liable for murder, even though it is reasonable to assume the action (a small push) would not cause death.

Theoretically there could be a suit involving the structure and safety of the motorcycle gas tank, but that seems unlikely. If your brother had a helmet cam with clear evidence of the accident the ham would be liable for all damage, regardless of the chain of cause. Your brother's bike continue to spin and hit someone? Liable. Your brother rolling around to put of the fire caused fire damage on someone's property? Liable. I dearly hope you took pictures of the scene, collected witness testimony and pray you have film evidence. Fatty can claim he drove into it and unfortunately motorcyclists are innately seen as more reckless and less sympathetic in the court system.

Record everything and save every document! Having a record of everything will never harm you and can be beneficial. The family time taken to visit your brother? The psychological stress brought to the family? Everything. Fatty could be liable for your father's heart attack bills if you can definitively prove the cause of injury was the motorcycle accident (this will be tough).

The court system is long and grueling. Just remember that your lawyer will be covered and fatty has to pay. This will take years to resolve, don't lose your resolve - fatty needs to pay. Be prepared to be a emotional glue to everyone, that role will fall on your (assuming you are the second oldest). You are the bridge between the children, the parents and your brother. Be prepared and be vigilant to your own needs, this will be a stressful 2-3 years for everyone. Good luck and I hope your brother can recover to normal.
